Proposed problem statement (confirmed behavior): Quick Swap lets a user replace a planned recipe on their weekly plan with another from their saved recipes in one or two taps; the swap preserves the plan slot and serving count, shows a confirmation toast, and only updates downstream systems (shopping list, nutrition totals, calendar) after the user confirms the swap.  
Open questions/trade-offs to resolve early: (1) should swaps default to “preserve side dishes/notes” or reset extras, (2) whether swaps should automatically update the shopping list (and be reversible), and (3) how to prioritize replacement suggestions (saved recipes first vs. algorithmic suggestions)—these affect UX copy, analytics needs, and edge-case handling.  
Proposed shared sequence (short, target 4-week flow we can stretch if needed): Day 0—30m kickoff with Design/Eng/Data/Marketing/Support; Days 1–4—Design drafts + initial interaction flows; Day 7—UX lock and Analytics event spec locked (Data + Eng sign-off); Day 8—Engineering kickoff and feasibility estimate; Days 9–21—implementation with weekly check-ins; Days 22–24—QA + analytics validation; Day 24—Marketing copy and Support docs finalized; Day 25–28—release window and monitoring.  
Decision owners at each point: Design locks interactions on Day 7, Data signs off on events Day 7, Engineering confirms schedule at kickoff and reports code-complete, Marketing locks naming/copy on Day 24, Support approves ops notes on Day 24.  
Next step: I’ll schedule the 30-minute kickoff for today—please confirm availability or propose an alternate time so we can commit to the Day 7 UX+analytics lock.
